questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{15}(6-x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<2 \\ h(x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1,\, & x>5.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2\le x\le 5,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ {\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{2}^{x}\frac{2}{15}(6-t)\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={-\frac{1}{15}t(t-12)|}_{2}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{15}x(x-12)-\frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{-{x}^{2}+12x-20}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ \frac{-{x}^{2}+12x-20}{15}, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{e}^{-|2x/3|}}{3},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}h(x),\, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2},\, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals.

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2x/3}}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{2x/3}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-2t/3}}{3}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{2x/3}}{2}, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-2x/3}}{2}, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{144}, & 0\le x\le 12 \\ 1, & x>12,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(4<X\le 6).$
questions.worked_solution:
We can perform this computation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(4<X\le 6) & =P(X\le 6)-P(X\le 4) \\  & =F(6)-F(4) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{2}}{144}-\frac{{4}^{2}}{144} \\  & =\frac{5}{36}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<4 \\ 1-\frac{16}{{x}^{2}}, & x\ge 4,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(X>6).$
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

Hence, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>6) & =1-P(X\le 6) \\  & =1-F(6) \\  & =1-(1-\frac{16}{{6}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{4{e}^{2x}}{(1+{e}^{2x})^{3}},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{4{e}^{2t}}{(1+{e}^{2t})^{3}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={-\frac{1}{(1+{e}^{2t})^{2}}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(1+{e}^{2x})^{2}}+1 \\  & =1-\frac{1}{(1+{e}^{2x})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
